newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Ousted Zaire cabinet urges army to stop fighting.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Zaire cabinet urges army to stop fighting.

text.p: The ousted government of radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi accused Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko of treason on Thursday and urged the army to stop fighting rebels who control half of the country.

A spokesman for the veteran Mobutu foe, speaking after a "cabinet" meeting in the garden of Tshisekedi's Kinshasa home, called for the ailing and embattled president to stand trial in the supreme court on charges of violating the constitution.
"Mr Mobutu, having illegally declared a state of emergency in Zaire, and appointed his prime minister illegally is guilty of high treason," spokesman Joseph Yaone said in a statement.

Mobutu, under growing international and domestic pressure to quit, shunted Tshisekedi aside on Wednesday, naming General Likulia Bolongo in what opponents say had all the hallmarks of a veiled coup. His army clashed with Tshisekedi loyalists trying to install their man in the prime minister's office complex.
Yaone urged Zaireans to step up efforts to oust Mobutu. "We are appealing to the people to intensify pressure of all sorts in order to force Mr Mobutu from power," he said.
"We are calling on the army to halt all fighting with the Allied Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire," Yaone added, referring to Laurent Kabila's rebels.
